title: Malaysia Refinery Operations
thesis: Snowflake turns daily unit data from a synthetic network of Malaysian refinery process units into yield-attainment KPIs, 7-day upset-risk scores, setpoint deviation anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Yield attainment, process upsets, energy intensity and charge processed for 24 process units across 5 Malaysian refinery sites.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to unit-day rows.
The product-shortfall chart shows which upset causes cost the most target product barrels.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of refinery KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which units are likely to have the next upset?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each unit's probability of a process upset in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags setpoint deviation outliers per unit, and the forecast projects network-wide yield attainment for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: How healthy are the units behind those risks?

talking_points: Unit availability and critical spares coverage frame the response capacity.
PM compliance against yield attainment by unit shows where discipline and yield move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, upset, cause and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a unit alarms right now?

talking_points: Live unit readings land in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, from the simulator or from AWS IoT Core through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ALARM readings with an SOP hint and the unit's current risk band, then emails the process engineer.
tabs.call_out: From alarm to action in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over synthetic SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (IoT Core, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
